name: 38451-prefill-moe-30b-dp4-ep
hardware: 4x H100 80GB HBM3, all four GPUs of one a3 node (--gres=gpu:4).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=4, expert parallelism ON so ep_size = dp x tp = 4 and the 128 experts split 32 per rank; four engine cores in one process group. Dual batch overlap ON, all2all on the DeepEP high-throughput kernels.
architecture: fine-grained sparse mixture-of-experts decoder (Qwen3MoeForCausalLM), FP8 weights, bf16 KV: 48 layers all sparse, 128 experts each, top-8 routing, 30.5B parameters and 3.3B active per token. The rest is in the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=64, warmup 16.67%, no cooldown, bounded at 768 requests with an 1800 s safety cap, static seed 38451. Read the measured request count off the run rather than deriving it from the bound.
workload: synthetic `synthetic_text`, single turn: 8192 prompt tokens and 1 output token per request, min == max == mean on both, `ignore_eos` set, `request_format: plain`. The engine adds a BOS, so the reported prompt count sits a token or two above 8192.
purpose: A document analysis service digesting 8,000-word submissions for 64 concurrent users on a sparse 30-billion-parameter model across four GPUs.
launch:
model: Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8

tensor-parallel-size: 1
data-parallel-size: 4
enable-expert-parallel: true

# The DeepEP high-throughput kernels are not the engine default and the python package they need
# is a build step -- see env.yaml.
all2all-backend: deepep_high_throughput

# Defaults to False at this commit and nothing turns it on implicitly; requires DP > 1.
enable-dbo: true

max-model-len: 32768

# Per engine core, so each of the four ranks admits 256.
max-num-seqs: 256

# PINNED DELIBERATELY -- do not drop it as "the default". Built in-process the unset argument
# resolves to 2048, not 8192, which would quarter the per-step token budget.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.9
enable-prefix-caching: false
